Team,

Attached is the consolidated Q3 budget summary for the group. As discussed at the close of last week, we need to begin shaping the Q4 ask well ahead of the usual cycle because of the lead times on equipment and the produce contracts expiring in Nov.

- Logistics (CoolChain) overran by more than we expected, mainly fuel and the rerouting around the Third Mainland Bridge closure.
- Labor costs stayed under budget, which is a win given the minimum wage adjustment mid-year.
- The VI branch and the Ikeja branch both came in under on consumables, which helped offset some of the overruns elsewhere.

A. Okafor
Finance Lead
Lagos Group Restaurants

Subject: BUDGET: Q3 file update and Q4 draft for review

All,

Attached are the updated Q3 file (v3) and the Q4 draft for review. I have incorporated the VI branch back office renovation as a separate line under branch improvements, per the receipts F. forwarded. The audit trail is complete.

The Q3 file now shows a total of 14,320,500 for the quarter, which is 320,500 over the original 14,000,000 budget. The overage is explained by the compressor repair (145,000), the renovation (89,500), and a fuel surcharge on the Lekki delivery van that came in at 86,000 (we had budgeted 60,000). The rest is minor line-item drift.

I will go through the line items at the meeting on Friday, but the summary is below for those who want to review before then.

Q3 SUMMARY (v3, final for reporting)
- Opening balance: 2,100,000
- Total revenue: 18,450,000
- Total food cost: 6,780,000
- Total labour: 5,120,000
- Total overheads: 2,420,500
- Net surplus: 4,129,500
- Closing balance: 6,229,500

The surplus is higher than the Q2 figure (3,210,000) mainly because the Lekki branch had a strong August (catering order for the law firm, 1.2m) and we did not repeat the equipment purchase we made in Q2.

Now for the Q4 draft. The total allocation is 18,000,000 as circulated. I have kept the same structure as Q3 but with the following changes:

1. Staffing: We are adding one junior line cook at the VI branch (from Nov 1) and one delivery rider for Lekki (from Oct 15). The rider is to cover the new catering contract we signed with the school in Yaba. That adds 780,000 for the quarter (cook 360,000, rider 240,000, plus employer pension/PAYE 180,000). Labour line goes from 5,120,000 to 5,900,000.

2. Marketing: We are moving 150,000 from the "print media" sub-line to "social media ads". The print vendor (Daily Times) has not been performing and the last two inserts did not run on the dates we paid for. I have a credit note for 80,000 from them and we will use it in Q1 next year. The social media agency has asked for a retainer increase of 50,000 per month, which is why the shift is needed. Total marketing remains 900,000.

3. Maintenance: The VI branch AC units need servicing before the harmattan. We have three quotes and the lowest is 210,000 for a full service of the four units. I have added a separate line "VI AC servicing" at 210,000 and reduced the general maintenance line from 350,000 to 250,000. Net maintenance total goes from 350,000 to 460,000.

4. Contingency: I have reduced this from 500,000 to 350,000. The reason is that the compressor repair and the renovation were both one-off items and we have no other known large expenses on the horizon. The Q3 overage was 320,500 and we still had 500,000 contingency, so we did not use it all. I think 350,000 is adequate. If anyone disagrees, pls say so at the meeting.

5. New line: "Catering equipment deposit" at 400,000. This is for the Yaba school contract. They require us to have a second warming cabinet and a chafing dish set before we start in November. The deposit is refundable but we need to pay it by Oct 20 to secure the equipment. I have attached the proforma invoice from the supplier (CoolKitchen Equipment).

The rest of the lines are unchanged from the draft I sent on Sep 26. The full draft is attached as a spreadsheet (Q4_draft_v2.xlsx). I have also attached a PDF version for those who prefer it.

One item I need to flag: the draft still shows the "new POS system" line at 650,000 for the Ikeja branch. This was in the original plan from August. I know we discussed delaying it because the current POS is working, but the vendor (SwiftPOS) has said the price will go up by 8% in November if we do not order this month. The 650,000 is the current price. If we delay, we will pay about 702,000. I have left it in the draft but marked it as "pending decision". Pls let me know your view.
